transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess I came in because I’m worrying about… everything, lately. I mean, I’ve always been someone who thinks things through—real estate kind of trains you to do that, you know, clients and the market and all the little details—but now it feels like it’s gotten bigger than what’s actually happening.

I’ll worry about a client not calling back, then suddenly I’m thinking about the whole market, or money, or my family, or whether moving to the condo was even the right decision. And then I’ll realize I’ve spent all this time going in circles over things that probably don’t need that much worry. It just feels out of proportion, I suppose.
When you start worrying, is it hard to stop or control it?

Yes, it is. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this is not urgent,” like I’m trying to be sensible about it, and for a minute I think I’ve put it aside. But then one thing connects to another.

Like, I might be thinking about one little detail from a client conversation, and then suddenly I’m replaying the whole thing, then wondering if I missed something, and before I know it I’ve spent half an hour on something I really meant to let go. It’s not always dramatic, but it’s hard to stop once it starts.
Have you been worrying like this most days for at least six months?

Yes… yes, I’d say so. It’s been more than six months. I think it really started after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo, which was—let me think—about a year and two months ago now.

That whole move was such a production, you know, sorting through years of things, and I kept telling myself I was downsizing and being practical. But since then, the worrying has just kind of stayed with me most days.
Do your worries feel mainly centered on the move to the condo and its aftermath?

Not mainly, no… I mean, the condo is part of it, definitely. I still wonder sometimes whether that was the right decision, and then I’ll think about all the things tied to that.

But it’s not just that. It spreads to clients, the market, my family, money—honestly, it feels like almost anything can become something to worry over. And the odd thing is, I can usually see that it’s bigger in my head than what’s actually happening, but that doesn’t always stop it.
Have you had sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that come on out of the blue?

Out of the blue… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t think I’ve had those dramatic, sudden attacks like you hear about where someone feels completely overcome all at once.

I do get worked up when my mind starts going—like if I’m thinking about a client issue or something with the condo board, and then it sort of builds. But it usually feels tied to something I’m already chewing on, not like it just drops out of the sky.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I’m not sure I’d say depressed, exactly. I mean, I have days where I feel worn out or discouraged, sure, but then I’ll get busy with work or talk to my daughter and it’s not like this heavy sadness that just sits there.

Although—well, winter always makes everything feel a little flatter to me, and the condo doesn’t get quite the same light my old house did in the afternoons. I used to love that, the way the sun came in the kitchen. But no, I don’t know that I’d call it feeling down in that way.
Do you often feel restless or keyed up?

Restless… maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d use that word. Keyed up, maybe more in the sense that I’m mentally “on,” like I should be checking something or thinking ahead.

But physically restless? I don’t know. I can sit through a showing or a meeting just fine. Although if it’s a slow open house, I’ll start tidying brochures or adjusting things on the counter—half the time that’s just habit, though. In real estate you’re always trying to make a place look just so. So… I’m not sure. What do you mean by keyed up exactly?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so… not in a clear way. I still like the things I like, I suppose. I mean, I don’t get to them as much as I used to, but that’s partly just life and work and, you know, keeping up with everything.

Like I used to spend more time gardening when I had the house, but in the condo it’s not really the same—there’s only so much you can do with a few pots on a balcony. I do still enjoy seeing my daughter, or going out to lunch if I actually make myself put it on the calendar. So… no, I haven’t really noticed losing interest, exactly.
Have you been feeling tired easily?

Tired easily… I’m not sure. I mean, I get tired, but I’m 61 and I’m still running around with clients, stairs, lockboxes, paperwork—half the time someone wants to see a place at the most inconvenient hour.

So I don’t know if it’s “easily” tired or just… normal tired. I do sometimes feel like I could sit down after a long day and not get back up for a while, but then I’ll remember I need to return a call or check an email, and I just keep going. I haven’t really thought of it as unusual, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Sleep… yes, that one I do notice. I usually get into bed at a reasonable time—I'm not up watching TV all night or anything—but then my mind starts going.

It’ll be condo fees, and then tomorrow’s showings, and then I’ll suddenly wonder if I missed some little detail in a contract. Which is silly sometimes, because I’ve checked it, but then I think, well, what if I didn’t check that one clause? And then I’m thinking about a buyer from three years ago who had an issue with an inspection, which has nothing to do with anything.

So it takes me a long time to really settle down. And even when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I didn’t quite… fully rest, if that makes sense.
Do you find it hard to concentrate because of the worrying?

Yes… I think so. Not all the time, but it happens when I’m trying to review something important, like a purchase agreement or an inspection addendum. I’ll be reading a paragraph and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether I forgot to call someone back, or whether there’s going to be some issue with a client, and then I realize I have no idea what I just read.

So I go back and read the same paragraph three or four times. Which is annoying, because those documents are already dry enough the first time through. But yes, the worrying does make me lose the thread sometimes.
Have you been feeling down or sad most days?

Down or sad most days… I don’t know that I’d put it that way. I mean, everybody has days where they’re a little worn out or discouraged, especially in real estate—one deal falls apart and then suddenly everyone’s calling like the roof is on fire.

But sad most days? I haven’t really noticed that as the main thing. I’m more… I don’t know, preoccupied, I guess. But not sitting around crying or feeling low every day, if that’s what you mean.
